questions.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy the first electron shell?
questions.explanation: The first electron shell can hold a maximum of 2 electrons. The second and third shells can hold up to 8 electrons each.

questions.stem: Sodium has an atomic number of 11. What is its electronic structure?
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons. These fill the shells in order: 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second shell, and 1 in the third shell, giving the electronic structure 2, 8, 1.

questions.stem: Which rule must be followed when filling electron shells?

options.text: Electrons fill the shells closest to the nucleus first
Electrons fill the outermost shell first
Electrons always go into the largest shell first

questions.explanation: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy level (closest to the nucleus) first before filling higher energy levels. This is because electrons at lower energy levels are more stable.

questions.stem: An element has the electronic structure 2, 8, 7. Which group of the Periodic Table does it belong to?
questions.explanation: The group number equals the number of electrons in the outer shell. This element has 7 electrons in its outer shell, so it belongs to Group 7 (the halogens).

questions.stem: Why do elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties?

options.text: Because they have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
Because they have the same total number of electrons
Because they have the same number of electron shells
Because they have the same number of neutrons

questions.explanation: Chemical properties are determined by the number of electrons in the outer shell. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer shell electrons, so they react in similar ways.

questions.stem: An atom has the electronic structure 2, 8, 8. What is its atomic number?
questions.explanation: The atomic number equals the total number of electrons in a neutral atom. Adding up the electrons: 2 + 8 + 8 = 18. This is argon, a noble gas.

questions.stem: Which of the following electronic structures represents a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Noble gases have full outer electron shells. The electronic structure 2, 8, 8 represents argon, which has a complete outer shell and is therefore very stable and unreactive.
